predecessors.note: The infobox lists the Tanjungpura Kingdom and the Mempawah Kingdom as predecessors; the founder came from Mempawah and married a daughter of the Panembahan of Mempawah. The page describes no land passing from Mempawah, so the handover is the founder's origin, not a transfer. Tanjungpura has no Cliopatria row or dossier.

successors.note: on 17 August 1950 the Republic of the United States of Indonesia dissolved and the Pontianak area became part of West Kalimantan Province.

correction.text: the Pontianak sultanate as a Dutch-protected sultanate inside the Dutch East Indies, outline of 1825-1827 unchanged

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Dutch East Indies shape from 1828 contains all 11 Pontianak cells, but the page has the sultanate continuing: Muhammad crowned 6 August 1895, the Japanese destroying the sultanate on 24 January 1944 and killing Muhammad on 28 June 1944, Hamid II crowned 29 October 1945, the Special Region of West Kalimantan formed on 28 October 1946, the infobox disestablishment year, 1950. The outline is carried on from the 1825 shape, drawn as a Dutch dependency inside the Dutch East Indies (the infobox status line (part of the Dutch East Indies from 1779)). No page opened gives its boundary after 1827; this is confidence 1. Re-read 2026-10-19: the West Kalimantan page gives the Special Region as 'established' on 12 May 1947 where the Pontianak page has 28 October 1946; the Special Region of West Kalimantan page (and Special_Region_of_West_Borneo) would not load, so the extent of the sultanate as a Dutch dependency 1828-1950 stays at confidence 1. The ledger now records the dependency as vassal_start 1800 / vassal_end December 1949 and the Japanese occupation 1942-1945 for this outline.

region.text: the site at 'the junction of the Landak River, Kapuas Kecil River, and Kapuas Besar River'

ledger.note: 23 October 1771: Syarif Abdurrahman Alkadrie founds Pontianak where the Landak, Kapuas Kecil and Kapuas Besar rivers meet. 'It was founded in 1771 by Sultan Syarif Abdurrahman Ibni Alhabib Husein bin Ahmad Alkadrie'; infobox establishment date 23 October 1771. He was confirmed as sultan in 1778 and endorsed by the VOC in 1779.

region.text: the Pontianak sultanate at the Kapuas mouth

ledger.note: 1800: the Pontianak sultanate is counted inside the Dutch East Indies as a protected sultanate. The page has the sultan endorsed 'by the Dutch East India Company in 1779', an agreement with the Sultan on 5 July 1779 over the inhabitants of Tanah Seribu, and an infobox status line 'Part of the Dutch East Indies (from 1779)'; the colony itself dates from 1800 (the VOC's end), so the tint starts there and the 1779 date is the page's. Mirrors dutch-east-indies /ledger/1 (vassal_start 1800, counterpart pontianak-kadriyah-sultanate).

1942: Japan occupies Pontianak. 'The era of Sultan Syarif Muhammad's reign faded quickly with the arrival of the Imperial Japanese army to Pontianak in 1942'; the page gives no month. The Japanese arrested the sultan's circle between September 1943 and early 1944 and, 'On 24 January 1944, considered rebellious and allied with the Dutch, the Japanese destroyed the Pontianak Sultanate', killing Sultan Syarif Muhammad on 28 June 1944. The Indies-wide occupation is in dutch-east-indies /ledger/52-59 (the navy's 2nd South Fleet held Borneo); counterpart here is the occupier, as in that dossier.

1945: the Japanese occupation of West Kalimantan ends. 'West Kalimantan was under Japanese occupation from 1942 to 1945, when Indonesia declared its Independence' (West Kalimantan page); the Pontianak page has Hamid II crowned on 29 October 1945. No month is given for Pontianak; the Indies-wide date is 15 August 1945 in dutch-east-indies /ledger/59.

December 1949: Dutch sovereignty over the Indies ends and the Pontianak sultanate stops being a Dutch dependency. The page has the Dutch-created Special Region of West Kalimantan formed on 28 October 1946, joining 'the Republic of Indonesia (RIS)' before 5 April 1950, and the sultanate disestablished in 1950; the December 1949 month is the Indies-wide transfer, not the page's. Mirrors dutch-east-indies /ledger/69 (vassal_end 1949-12, counterpart pontianak-kadriyah-sultanate).

17 August 1950: the Pontianak area passes to the Republic of Indonesia. On 17 August 1950 the RIS dissolved and the Pontianak area became part of West Kalimantan Province; the infobox gives 1950 as the year of disestablishment. Hamid II was later deposed over the APRA coup attempt (no date on the page). The page is not consistent on the exact step: 'Prior to 5 April 1950, the Special Region of West Kalimantan joined the Republic of Indonesia (RIS)' and 'After the dissolution of the Republic of Indonesia on 17 August 1950' the area became part of West Kalimantan Province, while the infobox says only 'Disestablished: 1950'. The August date is the RIS's end, not the sultanate's own, so the dissolve is kept at 17 August 1950 at confidence 2 (the West Kalimantan page gives 14 July 1950 for the province's establishment).

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary for the sultanate; the outline is Cliopatria's river-mouth shape and the Dutch dependency after 1828 is not surveyed on the page.

notes: Budget 1-2 pages: both used, the second (Dutch Borneo) was empty for this purpose. Cliopatria ends the row in 1827 and its Dutch East Indies shape from 1828 contains all 11 Pontianak cells; the page does not date or explain that (no 1818, 1822 or 1823 treaty on either page), so the 1828-1950 keyframe is a confidence-1 carry-forward of the sultanate as a Dutch dependency, justified only by the page's throne list and the infobox disestablishment year, 1950. The vassal tint for 1800-1949 is now recorded on both sides (repair of 2026-10-19): vassal_start 1800 and vassal_end December 1949 here, mirroring dutch-east-indies /ledger/1 and /ledger/69; the Japanese occupation 1942-1945 is recorded here too (counterpart empire-of-japan, the occupier, as in dutch-east-indies; empire-of-japan itself names dutch-east-indies for the whole Indies, so it has no event naming this slug). The sibling dossiers sultanate-of-sambas and sultanate-of-mempawah were ended at the Cliopatria years (1819, 1831) with the sultans noted as Dutch dependants; the orchestrator should decide whether Pontianak is drawn to 1950 or stops at 1827. Not settled: the 5 July 1779 agreement over Tanah Seribu (the Dutch 'used the land for their own activities', extent unstated); the Special Region of West Kalimantan (28 October 1946, a Dutch-created federal state) has no Cliopatria row and no dossier; the page says Pontianak came 'since 1811' into contact with the British without any territorial effect. A gap-filler should open 'Sultanate of Sambas' or 'Mempawah Kingdom' for the West Borneo events of 1818-1831. Repair of 2026-10-19: the Special Region of West Kalimantan page (and Special_Region_of_West_Borneo) did not load; the West Kalimantan page dates the Special Region to 12 May 1947 against 28 October 1946 on the Pontianak page. The 1950 dissolve is kept at confidence 2 because the page puts the region's joining of the RIS before 5 April 1950 and the RIS's end on 17 August 1950.
